$comment: LP FIDELITY LEDGER. Each entry is a geometric quantity measured on real LilyPond,
paired with the difference Lily# currently shows. See README.md for how to add or
regenerate an entry. The 'lilypond' numbers are DATA: they change only by re-running
the probes in probes/ against lilypond.exe and pasting what it prints.
residual = lilysharp - lilypond, in staff-spaces. A non-zero residual MUST carry a
'why'. Naming the defect is the goal; where it is not yet isolated, say so with an
'OPEN:' prefix and state exactly what is unexplained. What is forbidden is a silent
baseline. Both directions of change are failures: a residual that grows is a
regression, and a residual that shrinks is progress that must be recorded on purpose
so it appears in the diff rather than being absorbed.
The count of exact entries and the total |residual| are the headline fidelity numbers.

barline.next.down-stems-after-clef.why: Lily#'s stem-attachment inset (where the stem meets the notehead) differs from LilyPond's by ~7e-4 staff positions, and next_notes_correction divides the stem/bar-line overlap by 7. The sibling entry barline.next.down-stems is EXACT because there the bar line clips the stem's far end, so the attachment offset never enters the overlap — which localises this difference to that one metric rather than to the correction formula.

barline.next.accidental-to-notehead.why: Lily# spaces an accidental 1.300 from its notehead where LilyPond spaces it 1.450. The bar-line side of this same measure start is exact (barline.next.accidental), so the whole 0.150 is that accidental-to-head distance. Separate defect, not owned by Staff_spacing.

barline.next.key-change-glyph.why: LilyPond break-aligns a mid-line key change into the boundary column and spaces bar-line to key-signature by BarLine.space-alist (key-signature . (extra-space . 1.0)). Lily# has no such column and hangs the key signature off the following note column instead. COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 3.I / 4.3 #9.

barline.next.key-change-to-notehead.why: Same missing boundary column as barline.next.key-change-glyph: the whole prefix between bar line and note is priced by a different model. COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 3.I.

barline.next.time-change-glyph.why: Same missing boundary column: LilyPond spaces bar-line to time-signature by BarLine.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 0.75)). COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 3.I.

barline.next.time-change-to-notehead.why: Same missing boundary column as barline.next.time-change-glyph. COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 3.I.

midmeasure.clef.prev-note-to-clef.why: Change items are measured from their CENTRE (width/2 + ClefChangePadding) in all three extent helpers, so a mid-measure clef sits too far right inside the gap it shares. COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 4.7 item 1. Note the SIGN against its sibling midmeasure.clef.clef-to-next-note: the two sides of the same glyph are wrong in OPPOSITE directions, which is the signature of a frame error rather than of a wrong constant — a wrong constant would push both the same way.

midmeasure.clef.clef-to-next-note.why: Other side of midmeasure.clef.prev-note-to-clef; see the note there. The note-to-note total is also 1.119 too wide, so this is not purely a placement-within-the-gap problem.

midmeasure.key.prev-note-to-key.why: Same centre-basis frame as midmeasure.clef.prev-note-to-clef. COORDINATE_AUDIT.md 4.7 item 1.

midmeasure.key.key-to-next-note.why: Other side of midmeasure.key.prev-note-to-key. Here the note-to-note total is only 0.451 too wide while the change glyph is 2.45 out of place, so for a key change the error is almost entirely WHERE the glyph sits in the gap rather than how wide the gap is.

barline.prev.whole-note.why: OPEN: not yet attributed. The closing gap of a whole-note measure is 0.002 narrow. A whole note has no stem, so no optical correction is involved; the suspects are the duration-space formula and the notehead-advance metric. Too small to see in SVG output, which rounds to two decimals — this entry exists precisely because that rounding hid it (the earlier note was 'LP 4.098045 vs Lily# 4.10').

barline.prev.half-note.why: OPEN: not yet attributed, and probably the same cause as barline.prev.whole-note — both are closing gaps that are ~0.001-0.002 narrow while every opening gap in this corpus is exact. Note this one DOES carry a stem correction, so if the two share a cause it is not the optical term.
